title: Shavuot: a night of learning
hookLine: staying up to learn, even an hour past your bedtime
tomorrow: why does every chapter of Avot start with a borrowed line?

cards: The alarm goes off once. Nobody moves. It goes off again.
Still nothing. Usually that means a missed first period. In this story, it's the morning God is about to speak at Sinai.
A midrash tells it plainly: on the morning the Torah was given, the people were still asleep, and they had to be woken up. So why would anyone stay up all night on purpose?
To make sure that this time, nobody sleeps through it.

teach.b: Exodus makes that morning loud: "And it came to pass on the third day, when it was morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of a horn exceeding loud."
And still, says the midrash, the people had slept in. It's a strangely human detail to keep about the biggest morning in the story.

teach.h: TIKKUN: THE REPAIR OF THE NIGHT.
teach.b: Later Jews answered it with a custom: tikkun leil Shavuot, the repair of Shavuot night.
Some stay awake on the first night of the festival, learning until dawn, in a synagogue, a living room, a kitchen with too much coffee.
Kabbalists in Safed shaped a set reading for the night, passages from the Torah, the Prophets and the Mishnah.
Now it might be a string of short classes, a study partner, or one good page. The repair is the point. Last time they slept; this time we're up, waiting.
You don't need the whole night.
Even an hour past your bedtime, reading something that matters, on purpose, while the house is dark, is the same gesture in small: I'm here, I'm awake, I don't want to miss it.

how: On the first night of Shavuot, some Jews stay awake learning Torah until dawn, alone, with a partner, or at a synagogue program of short classes; others learn for an hour or two past their usual bedtime.

o: staying up on Shavuot night to learn, as a repair
a vigil kept beside someone who has just died
a fast on the eve of Shavuot to prepare the body

games.q: the night of learning — tap the pairs.

s: the people at Sinai stayed up all night, waiting
the midrash says they slept in and had to be woken; the night of learning repairs that.
tikkun leil Shavuot: the repair of Shavuot night.
the Torah commands staying up all night on Shavuot
it's a later custom. Exodus gives the morning of thunder; the midrash gives the oversleeping.

games.q: your friend hosts a Shavuot night study. most people can only stay till midnight. she asks if she should cancel. what fits the custom?
o: keep it: even an hour awake on purpose is the gesture.
cancel: the custom only counts if it lasts until dawn.
keep it, but swap the learning for a movie so people stay.
games.why: the repair is being awake for the gift. the whole night is the custom's full form; an hour of real learning is the same gesture, smaller.

practice: Copy one line by hand from any book that matters to you, slowly, word by word, the way you'd copy a recipe you don't want to lose. Read it back once, quietly. That's the night of learning, in miniature.

wordCard.voice: Tikkun leil Shavuot: the repair of Shavuot night, staying up to learn so that, this time, no one sleeps through the gift.

orig.note: Hebrew: repair, setting right; the name of the Shavuot night of learning.

carryVoice: Hold this one close: awake for the gift, even for one extra hour. Good night, and good morning.
